notes: Extended from the supplied graph. The supplied edges office_a_entry-office_a, office_b_entry-office_b and meeting_room_entry-meeting_room passed through the yellow cylinder, green ball and blue box, so each now goes through an *_inner node.

office_a_entry and office_b_entry moved from y=0.75 to y=0.55: at 0.75 the edge to centre_north passed 0.14 m from the partition corner, close enough for the 45-degree proximity sensors to stop the robot.

centre-centre_north is kept although it crosses BLOCKING_OBSTACLE: the specification calls that obstacle movable, so the robot must discover it with its proximity sensors. The two centre_bypass nodes give a route around it after it is detected.

*_far nodes are third search viewpoints behind the furniture (lab bench, office desks, meeting table). A 2-D line-of-sight check showed 8-23% of each room's floor was hidden from the first two viewpoints; each *_far spot was chosen to see most of that strip and to be reachable in a straight line with 0.18 m clearance.
office_a_entry-centre and office_b_entry-centre: direct links so trips between an office and the south side do not have to pass centre_north and go round BLOCKING_OBSTACLE.

backup_edges: the internal doors in the walls at y=0 (lab <-> office A at x=-3.6, meeting room <-> office B at x=3.6). Used only when no route exists without them (e.g. a room's main doorway is blocked). Each path keeps at least 0.19 m from walls, furniture and all ball spawn positions.
